transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've asked us to meet today to discuss the first-year composition program's proposal to pilot an AI writing-feedback platform in two sections next term. As I understand it, the platform can generate comments on student drafts and can be configured for different levels of instructor control. Before I make a decision on whether this pilot may proceed and under what conditions, I'd like to hear from the relevant parties. Our routine review process asks the writing program and the privacy office to report any instructional or data-handling requirements before an academic technology pilot is approved. Could we start with the writing program's perspective on the instructional considerations, and then hear from the privacy office on any data concerns?

transcript.text: I should note that this week I finalized our writing program's adopted pilot standard for AI feedback platforms. The standard permits the platform only for formative feedback, requires an instructor to review every generated suggestion before it is released to a student, and prohibits using the platform to assign or determine grades. This standard has not yet been added to the proposal packet, so I want to make sure everyone here is aware of it as we discuss the pilot.

transcript.text: I should share the results of my completed vendor review. The review found that approval requires institutional single sign-on and a signed addendum stating that the vendor retains no student prompts or submissions. The vendor has confirmed it will accept those terms. However, I want to note that the review memo is still awaiting attachment to the proposal packet, so it hasn't been formally included yet.
